policy.redirect_referer.reason: Go's net/http sets Referer on a followed redirect; simple_http does not. RFC 9110 §10.1.4 makes the field optional, and omitting it is the privacy-preserving choice.

policy.redirect_cross_origin.reason: Go's http.Client decides whether to forward Authorization/Cookie on a redirect by hostname only, ignoring the port; simple_http compares the full origin (scheme+host+port) per RFC 9110 §4.3.1 and strips them across a port change. The library is stricter and matches the origin boundary.

h3.status_204.reason: quic-go's HTTP/3 reference server emits Content-Length: 0 on a 204 (it fills Content-Length after the handler returns without excluding bodyless statuses). RFC 9110 §8.6 forbids Content-Length on a 204, and nghttp3 deliberately removes that field from the response header list (it tolerates the invalid value 0 on the wire but does not surface it), so simple_http reports framing=none while Go reports content-length. The C++ behavior is the RFC-aligned one.

raw.cl_te.reason: Go net/http accepts a request carrying both Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding (TE wins); simple_http rejects the double framing with 400 per RFC 9112 §6.3 and as a request-smuggling defense.

raw.duplicate_cl.reason: Go net/http collapses/accepts duplicate identical Content-Length values; simple_http rejects duplicate Content-Length with 400 per RFC 9112 §6.3 (ambiguous framing / smuggling vector).

raw.obs_fold.reason: Go net/http accepts obsolete line folding in a header value; simple_http rejects it with 400. RFC 9112 §5.2 obsoletes obs-fold and permits rejecting it; rejecting avoids front-end/back-end smuggling splits.

body.request_trailers_h3.reason: C++ HTTP/3 request trailers are not exposed to handlers (documented limitation: only h1/h2 expose Request::trailers()); Go's quic-go server forwards them to r.Trailer, so /trailer-echo answers yes there and missing here. The case pins the limitation rather than hiding it.
